# Metaplate v0.8.0

Metaplate 0.8 lets applications run a current Satori without waiting for a Metaplate release, names the font descriptor type that declaration builds were missing, and moves the framework evidence forward to React Router 8 and Vite 8. Nothing in the public API is removed or tightened: every 0.7 plate, route, and CLI invocation keeps working unchanged.

> **Upgrade recommendation:** Recommended for every 0.7 user, especially projects that already depend on a newer Satori, emit TypeScript declarations that mention font descriptors, or run React Router 8. There is no migration.

## Why upgrade

The `satori` peer range in 0.7 stopped at `<0.34`. Satori publishes a new minor version for each feature without recording breaking changes, so applications that took a current Satori, or another library that required one, hit npm peer conflicts against Metaplate within days of each Satori release. Version 0.8 accepts `>=0.33.3 <1` and is audited against Satori 0.63.2, which also bundles its own layout engine so `yoga-layout` leaves the installed tree.

Projects that build declaration files from code that returns or re-exports a font descriptor could fail with TS2742 because the shared descriptor shape had no public name. It is now exported as `FontFace`.

The release also documents two rendering behaviors that previously surprised users, React fragments on older Satori and Node-rendered JPEG or WebP cards inside Next.js 16, and runs the React Router resource-route fixture on React Router 8.

## Highlights

### Current Satori releases without peer conflicts

- The `satori` peer range widens from `>=0.33.3 <0.34` to `>=0.33.3 <1`. Applications can move to Satori 0.63.x, which contains 0.63.2, the audited release. A fresh `npm install metaplate@0.8.0` resolves the newest Satori 0.x release, and earlier releases from 0.33.3 on remain inside the range. See the [Satori releases](https://github.com/vercel/satori/releases) for upstream changes.
- Satori 0.38.2 and newer flatten a React fragment like the DOM does. On older Satori a fragment is laid out as a zero-sized box of its own, so absolutely positioned children anchor to that box and full-bleed backgrounds can be clipped without any error. The [plate constraints](https://github.com/lnorton89/metaplate/blob/v0.8.0/README.md#plate-constraints) now explain the difference, and a test pins the current behavior. The documented workaround, rendering such children directly instead of inside a fragment, only matters when a deployment can resolve a Satori release older than 0.38.2.

### Typed font descriptors

- `metaplate/fonts` and `metaplate/font-data` export `FontFace`, the base shape shared by `DataFont`, `FileFont`, `PackageFont`, and `FontsourceFont`. Code that annotates or re-exports a font descriptor can now name it, and declaration builds no longer stop with TS2742.

### Framework guidance and evidence

- JPEG and WebP cards in Next.js: [JPEG or WebP cards in Next.js](https://github.com/lnorton89/metaplate/blob/v0.8.0/README.md#jpeg-or-webp-cards-in-nextjs) shows how to use `metaplate/node` in a Next.js 16 route handler. Turbopack cannot bundle Resvg's native binary or Satori's HarfBuzz WebAssembly, so both are listed in [`serverExternalPackages`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverExternalPackages), and naming the route folder after `imagePath` (for example `og-image.jpg/`) gives a [static export](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/static-exports) a real file extension. Tested boundary: `metaplate/next` on Next.js 16.3.2 to 16.x on the Node/build pipeline; the `metaplate/node`-in-Next recipe is documentation, not a separate release fixture.
- React Router: the packed-artifact fixture now builds, serves, and fetches a dynamic [resource route](https://reactrouter.com/how-to/resource-routes) `loader(args)` on React Router 8 and Vite 8, and still fails if React Router emits Vite's deprecated `envFile` warning. Tested boundary: React Router 8 framework mode on Node 22.22 or newer.
- Astro: the [static endpoint](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/endpoints/) fixture is unchanged in shape. Tested boundary: Astro 7 build on Node 24.
- Edge runtimes remain unsupported for the native renderer, and hosted provider certification is still not claimed: deployment evidence is local packed-contract evidence only.

### Toolchain and reliability

- Metaplate is now built and type-checked with TypeScript 6.0, tsup 9, and vitest 5. tsup 9 no longer injects the deprecated `baseUrl` option into its declaration build, so the published declarations need no deprecation escape hatch, and vitest 5 clears the `@vitest/mocker` advisory from the development tree.
- The package still supports Node 20 or newer at runtime; the Node 20 compatibility job runs the new toolchain and passes. The full local release gate needs Node 22.23.4 or newer because its packed-package fixtures build real Astro 7.4 and React Router 8 apps.

## Breaking changes

None.

## Install or upgrade

```sh
npm install metaplate@0.8.0
```

That single command still includes the framework-neutral SVG and PNG renderer.
The only peer-range change is `satori`, which widens to `>=0.33.3 <1`. New
installs resolve the newest Satori 0.x release (0.63.2, the audited release,
when 0.8.0 was prepared), while npm keeps an existing Satori that already
satisfies the range. To move an existing project to the audited line, run
`npm install satori@0.63` alongside the upgrade. Next applications continue to
supply their own compatible `next` dependency.

## Verification

- `npm run check` passes lint, a zero-tolerance duplication scan, workflow pin policy, dependency inventory and Socket disposition policy, deployment evidence policy, release-note validation, source and example type checks, 378 tests, build, and a 33-file package dry run (one fewer than 0.7.0: tsup 9 no longer emits a private `font-data` declaration chunk because `fonts.d.ts` now imports `FontFace` from the public entry).
- `npm run check:package` exercises the exact local tarball: lean and standalone consumers, offline Next static export, Astro 7 static build, Express service, React Router 8 resource route, and the Vercel `handlerFrom`, Vercel Fetchable, and Netlify `context.params` deployment fixtures with image and response-header evidence.
- `npm run release:evidence` re-runs the build, packed-artifact, inventory, deployment, Socket, and workflow checks, records each result with captured output, and binds the bundle, including the SHA-256 of every evidence artifact, to the release commit.
- The Socket baseline is the official Socket CLI deep score of the published `metaplate@0.7.0` package, captured 2026-10-31 (`socket package score npm metaplate@0.7.0 --json`) and imported through the repository's importer, which re-derives every alert's dependency evidence from the lockfile. The package itself scores 80 overall with no alerts; its full dependency graph scores 38 overall across 90 packages with 20 alerts, none critical. The two high alerts carry time-bounded `accepted-with-evidence` dispositions that expire 2027-04-30: the `string.prototype.codepointat` maintenance upgrade signal under the Satori peer (unchanged since 0.6.0), and the `unstableOwnership` signal on `tslib@2.9.1`, whose publisher moved to Microsoft's npm identity on 2026-10-30 with the TypeScript team maintainers retained and the upstream tag and release in place; tslib is reached only through the optional `next` peer and the development-only Astro fixture, never through the required renderer peers. The 0.8.0 release itself has not been scored by Socket yet, because Socket scores published packages. `npm audit` results are not a substitute for Socket's behavioral and native-code analysis.
- npm registry signature and SLSA provenance verification run automatically after publication and remain the final release check because they cannot execute before the public artifact exists.
